analysis.title: European Morning Note
key_insights: FOMC held rates at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote. Cook and Hammack dissented in favour of a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded its assessment of activity from "solid" to "strong" and said incoming data will determine the policy stance.
Chair Warsh was hawkish. He cited stronger growth, elevated inflation, robust productivity and double-digit investment growth, and reiterated the 2% inflation target.
US stocks closed higher on Wednesday, with the S&P +0.3% and the Nasdaq +0.5%. VGZ6 (Euro Stoxx 50 futures) was +0.1% in early trading.
Alphabet fell 10% after hours on a miss in Search. The note says AI cannibalisation concerns are back at the centre of the debate.
Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours. Azure growth printed 48%, a 3ppt beat.
Oracle rose 10% after hours. CFO Maxson guided free cash flow to turn positive in 2H28 and to top $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines.

Asia was mixed. The KOSPI was lower as Samsung (-5%) reversed an initially positive reaction to results. Japan was flat ahead of the Topix rebalance. China was softer on mixed earnings and tech read-across, with China semis -3% and Hong Kong tech lower across the board.
Crude fell 1.4% to WTI $101.3 and Brent $113.7, easing from the prior day's best levels.
The UBS London sales desk saw a strong European buyside bias of more than $2bn across the major EU indexes on Wednesday, and continued buying of MES after the weekend weakness.
Data due today: US Personal Income (Sep) 0.3% at 12:30, US Initial Jobless Claims 198K at 12:30, US Q3 GDP annualized QoQ 3.2% at 12:30, and the ECB rate decision at 13:15.
